Help.Cli.Title: Command Line Interface
Help.Cli.Description: The following commands can be used in chat or your macro text.
Help.Clicks.Title: Click Commands
Help.Clicks.Description: Click commands can be used to interact with game UI elements. You can use these in your macros.
Help.Clicks.RedNote: Items in red are properties that themselves have methods (not callable directly).
Help.Keys.Title: Virtual Keys
Help.Keys.Description: Use the /send command to simulate keyboard input. This is useful for interacting with UI elements that don't have dedicated click commands.
Help.Lua.Title: Lua Scripting
Help.Lua.Description: Below are all of the functions and properties provided by the framework. Click any to copy the full call path to clipboard. Hover any function to learn more about it.
Help.General.Intro1: {0} is an expansion of the native macro system, with smart helpers, additional commands and modifiers, and unlimited macros.
Help.General.Intro2: It also supports scripting with Lua, so you can write macros that are more complex than the native system can handle.
Help.General.StatusDescription: That status window shows all currently running macros and their current state
Help.General.State.Ready: Ready: Macro has been loaded but hasn't started running
Help.General.State.Paused: Paused: Macro execution has been temporarily stopped
Help.General.State.Failed: Failed: Macro encountered an error during execution
Help.General.Triggers.Intro: Macros can be configured to trigger automatically based on specific game events:
Help.General.Triggers.Lua: Lua macros can also be configured to have individual functions trigger automatically (provided the script was already running).
Help.General.Triggers.Register: Any function that begins with the name of a TriggerEvent will be registered in the {0} when the script is started.
Help.General.Triggers.Addon: For {0} specifically, the event name must be followed by the addon name and event type, such as
Help.General.Metadata.1: Macros can be configured with metadata to provide specific configurations to the framework regarding macro execution.
Help.General.Metadata.2: The metadata can be edited in the Macros Settings section when a macro is selected in the library.
Help.General.Metadata.3: The metadata can be written to the file using the button provided in the above section. This is crucial for macros stored remotely (i.e. github) for the framework to know what settings to use when they're imported
Help.General.Deps.1: Macros can also be configured to require other plugins to run, and a message will be printed if the requirement is not met.
Help.General.Deps.2: Similiarly, macros can be configured to disable other plugins while running, though this requires plugins to be pre-defined in the framework to support this.
Help.General.Deps.3: Like plugin dependencies, macros can support relying on other macros, whether they're local (already loaded into snd) or remote (i.e. github)
Help.General.Git.1: Macros can now be connected to a github url and auto converted into a "Git Macro"
Help.General.Git.2: Git macros support auto updating when a new version is released (checked on startup), and going between versions via the version history modal (found in the Macro Settings section)
Help.General.Git.3: A macro is automatically identified as a git macro when it has a repository url in its metadata. To convert a git macro back into a local macro, simply wipe the url or click the Reset Git Data button in the settings
Cmd.MainHelp: Open a window to edit various settings.
Cmd.Run: Run a macro, the name must be unique.
Cmd.RunLoop: Run a macro and then loop N times, the name must be unique.
Cmd.PauseLoop: Pause the given executing macro at the next loop point.
Cmd.StopLoop: Stop the given executing macro at the next loop point.
Cmd.Id: Get the macro ID for a macro name.
Cmd.InvalidLoop: Invalid loop command format. Usage: /snd run loop <count> "<macro name>"
